## TC Energy outlines next phase of NGTL System growth


*Proposed Alberta Growth Connector and new service offerings will create scalable capacity to meet accelerating demand across Alberta*


CALGARY, Alberta, Nov. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- TC Energy Corporation (TSX, NYSE: TRP) (TC Energy or the Company) today shared its next phase of growth on its NGTL System, including plans for the proposed Alberta Growth Connector, an approximately 370-kilometre, 48-inch, west-to-east natural gas pipeline that would connect growing Western Canadian natural gas supply directly to Alberta’s oil sands region via NGTL.


The NGTL Annual Plan provides an NGTL supply and demand forecast and identifies the related infrastructure needs. The 2026 NGTL System Annual Plan is expected to be filed with the federal regulator by year end then publicly released. It is subject to finalization and outlines the next phase of growth for the five-year planning horizon (2026-2031). The plan forecasts total demand on the system will increase approximately 25 per cent over the next five years, from 14.4 billion cubic feet per day (Bcf/d) in 2026 to approximately 18 Bcf/d in 2031.


The updated forecast draws on customer discussions, Expressions of Interest, recent service offering results and broader market fundamentals. The 2031 forecast is approximately 1.5 Bcf/d higher than the outlook presented in the 2025 NGTL System Annual Plan, reflecting demand growth that has accelerated over the past year. More than 60 per cent of the forecast increase is expected to come from Alberta’s oil sands, power generation and data centre sectors.


“Growing natural gas demand across Alberta reinforces NGTL’s role as a foundational part of TC Energy’s business and a core platform for future growth,” said François Poirier, TC Energy’s President and Chief Executive Officer. “The Alberta Growth Connector would leverage our extensive existing network to connect growing supply with growing demand, initially adding approximately one billion cubic feet per day of capacity with the ability to expand further as customer needs develop.”


The Alberta Growth Connector would form part of a broader proposed facility plan that includes additional pipeline loops and compressor units across the integrated NGTL-ATCO System. The project is designed to increase operational flexibility and establish a scalable foundation for future capacity additions through compression.


Next steps will include launching additional service offerings as early as January 2027, giving customers another opportunity to contract for incremental service, which could exceed 1.3 Bcf/d of new delivery service between 2030 and 2032. This builds on the approximately 1 Bcf/d of incremental service offered in 2026.


“We are working closely with customers to develop the commercial case required to advance the next phase of NGTL growth, including the proposed Alberta Growth Connector,” said Poirier. “Our approach is deliberate and disciplined: leverage our existing infrastructure, align investment with customer commitments and advance projects that meet our risk and return requirements.”


Over the past decade, TC Energy has invested more than $15 billion in the NGTL System, increasing its rate base from approximately $6 billion to nearly $19 billion and expanding capacity to more than 18 Bcf/d. The company is also advancing approximately $1.2 billion of sanctioned NGTL expansion projects.


The proposed Alberta Growth Connector and related facilities remain subject to securing commercial support, engagement with rightsholders and stakeholders, regulatory approvals and TC Energy’s project-sanctioning process.


“The strength of our footprint gives us a significant advantage as natural gas and power demand grows,” added Poirier. “By expanding an established integrated network, we can add capacity efficiently and advance high-quality, in-corridor growth that creates long-term value for customers and shareholders.”


**About TC Energy**
We are a leader in North American energy infrastructure, spanning Canada, the U.S. and Mexico. For over 75 years, we have proudly connected the world to the energy it needs. Every day, we move more than 30 per cent of the natural gas used across the continent and connect LNG exports to global markets—powering communities and industries. Complemented by strategic ownership and low-risk investments in power generation, our infrastructure delivers affordable, reliable and sustainable energy across North America.


We carry forward a legacy of nation-building energy infrastructure and strong partnerships. By working with communities, businesses and leaders across our extensive energy network, we create opportunities today and for generations to come.


TC Energy’s common shares trade on the Toronto (TSX) and New York (NYSE) stock exchanges under the symbol TRP. To learn more, visit us at[TCEnergy.com](https://www.tcenergy.com/) .
